title: Building a Resilient Supply Chain for Complex IVD Reagents (or Proteins)
summary: Explore expression hurdles and scale-up delays in IVD antigens and enzymes. Learn how whole-insect biomanufacturing secures resilient supply.
body_markdown:
## Introduction


In the world of in vitro diagnostics (IVD), recent global market disruptions make one truth clear: a diagnostic test is only as reliable as its underlying supply chain. When critical antigens suffer from supply shortages, lot-to-lot inconsistencies, or scale-up hurdles, the consequences go beyond manufacturing delays to increased cost of goods and compromised patient care.


As demand for advanced diagnostics expands across point-of-care testing, disease detection, and personalized medicine, manufacturers face mounting pressure to secure high-quality assay proteins that scale reliably.1 ,2 For those working with complex or specialized antigens or enzymes, traditional biological sourcing puts commercial timelines at risk and remains a significant challenge.


In order to build a more resilient supply chain, assay developers must rethink how critical protein reagents are produced and move beyond native biological sources towards scalable recombinant expression platforms.
